question: Decision 1: who holds sellers' money between the buyer's payment and the seller's payout?
decision: C, with the three defaults, in every market at launch. Each payment method's provider holds the money, in the seller's own account with that provider; for cash on delivery the seller's courier holds it until it settles with the seller; paid by transfer or in cash, it goes to the seller. (1) An account a seller requests through Sharrwah but holds under its own agreement with the provider counts as C; one where Sharrwah would be party to the money, or to the provider's agreement for it, is B and comes to the founder. (2) Sharrwah's fees are billed apart, never taken from sellers' money at a provider. (3) No balance that sellers pay into. A and B stay off: building or switching on either is the founder's decision (the guard)

question: Sharrwah's intent: what the platform is, where its extent comes from, and who decides what
decision: Sharrwah is a merchant platform of the established class that Shopify represents worldwide and Salla and Zid in the region. It is meant to grow into that class's full maturity across MENA, one market after another as resources and teams for each market's deals allow. Yemen is the first market set up on it. Its extent comes from the class, not from the launch. What the class establishes, and the slots it leaves for outside parties, belong to the platform. What fills a slot in a market (its providers, partners and law) is that market's setup, needed when the slot is filled; it never defines the platform. Engineering establishes from the references' evidence what is common, how it fits together, where variation is genuine, which shape is better where they differ, and which commitments keep growth open. Launch and today's resources decide when, never whether. I decide which markets, in what order and when, and which merchants Sharrwah goes after first; plans and prices; commercial agreements and partners; the company, its legal structure and licences; spending; and whether Sharrwah's own company runs a service in the merchant's business (payments, balances, financing, shipping, a marketplace, point of sale, data services), where and when. Sharrwah rules out nothing the class shows; the platform keeps room for each of these, whoever provides it. Everything else is engineering's, and I may veto any of it. The test for any work: narrowing what the class establishes needs a decision of mine or an engineering reason with evidence. Ordering it is ordinary engineering. (The founder's heading to it:) It takes in the scope decision of 28 October; where an earlier decision differs, this one holds. Added on review, in the coordinator's wording, which the founder accepted, with the founder's edits to the first and the fourth: (1) A need one of my markets shows that the class doesn't meet is a product gap: building it goes with that market's setup, and it never defines the platform. How the platform keeps room for it is engineering's. (2) In my list of services, the decision is whether Sharrwah's own company operates the service in the merchant's business (payments, balances, financing, shipping, a marketplace, point of sale, data services, a buyer app), where and when. The platform's capabilities for each remain the class's. (3) [Taken out by the founder on 30 October (the row of that day): what keeping room means is engineering's, stated in the architecture plan.] (4) My decision of 28 October stays in force where this one doesn't restate it (https://github.com/Hamza-ye/sharrwah-knowledge-map/blob/537ddb771587ce173e930508e3683eaaddc4c995/founder-decisions.tsv?plain=1#L25). A standing decision
basis: The founder's handoff of 29 October 2026, verbatim: founder-messages/2026-10-29-intent-handoff.md; the coordinator's review, which proposed the added lines: reports/intent-review.md, sections 5 and 10; the founder's go with edits, verbatim: founder-messages/2026-10-29-go.md
